name: Is it better to build the pool first or the whole backyard at once?

mainEntity.name: Should the pool be built first or should the whole backyard be built at the same time?
mainEntity.text: Should the pool be built first or should the whole backyard be built at the same time?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most Los Angeles projects, building the pool and the surrounding backyard at the same time is the smarter option because the layout, elevations, drainage, lighting, gas, and irrigation all need to work together. If the pool is completed first and the rest of the yard comes later, crews may have to cut into finished concrete, relocate utilities, or adjust elevations that were never coordinated in the first place. That usually increases cost and can create a less seamless final result. A phased approach can make sense if the budget is tight or if the homeowner wants to complete the pool before adding landscaping or a kitchen, but the design should still account for the future phases. The best practice is to plan the entire site at once, even if construction happens in stages. That gives the contractor and designer a chance to preserve access, protect drainage, and avoid expensive rework.
acceptedAnswer.description: Building the pool and the rest of the backyard together is usually better because it improves layout coordination, avoids tearing up finished hardscape later, and reduces conflicts between drainage, utilities, and patio elevations. Separate phases can work, but they often increase cost and rework.
